item.title: [7] Anomalous metal and superconducting phases in rhombohedral graphene
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Joshua Folk, Matthew Yankowitz

Authors: Anna Okounkova, Abigail Sohm, Tobias Faehndrich, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Superconducting and anomalous metal phases in rhombohedral graphene, a relevant 2D material.

Tags: #graphene #superconductivity #2Dmaterials #vanderWaals

Abstract: Observations of rhombohedral graphene on a WSe2 substrate at varying temperature, magnetic field and current indicate the presence of regions of gate space with zero-resistance superconductivity alongside others with finite saturation resistance.

item.title: [7] Stacking-induced direct band gap in CVD-grown 1H MoS2 bilayers
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Kuang-I Lin, Yann-Wen Lan

Authors: Tilo H. Yang, I-Tong Chen, Min-Jia Zhang, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Electronic structure modification in 2D MoS2 bilayers relevant for optoelectronics and valleytronics.

Tags: #2Dmaterials #MoS2 #electronicstructure #valleytronics

Abstract: Atomically aligned 1H bilayer MoS2 exhibits a direct band gap, enhanced excitonic emission and stronger valley polarization, establishing its potential for advanced optoelectronic and valleytronic applications.

item.title: [7] Organic two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Thomas Heine, Xinliang Feng

Authors: Anupam Prasoon, Nguyen Ngan Nguyen, Mike Hambsch, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Study of van der Waals heterostructures, relevant to 2D materials and condensed matter.

Tags: #materials #2Dmaterials #heterostructures

Abstract: Sequential on-water-surface assembly enables layer-by-layer stacking of two-dimensional polymers to create both lattice-matched and controlled lattice-mismatched van der Waals heterostructures with defined lattice registry, stacking sequence and thickness.

item.title: [6] Efficient yet stable large perovskite solar modules made using surface treatment
item.content:encoded:
Authors: Authors not available in source RSS

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Materials science of perovskite solar cells, generally relevant to quantum materials.

Tags: #materials #perovskites #energy

Abstract: Non-uniformities in the layer of passivator molecules, which are used to fix defects and protect the surface of perovskite material in solar cells, can limit the durability of the resulting modules. Large modules treated instead with chemically stable lead carboxylate passivators were efficient, reliable and had a higher yield than did commercial silicon modules.

item.title: [7] There’s a new form of boron — and it’s really weird
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Dhruv Shenai

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Discovery of a new boron phase with unusual conductivity, potentially relevant to electronic properties.

Tags: #materials #electronicproperties #highpressure

Abstract: A boron phase prepared under pressure is a million times more conductive than chemists expected, and can be stretched.
